audit_findings.title: Facility construction may contaminate normalized owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.765m of 2025 property-and-equipment purchases and approximately $15.2m total filed construction cost; the 2025 purchases equal 45.4% of the $17.1m anchor and, as an upper-bound permanent adjustment, compute to about $121.7m or $9.41/share of BASE value
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor may deduct nonrecurring expansion construction as maintenance capital expenditure, while excluding all construction requires a separate allowance for recurring facility maintenance.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025 and 2024, cash outflows were primarily the cost of our new corporate office and manufacturing facility in Orlando, Florida, which is now completed and occupied.
audit_findings.explanation: The facility expenditure is filed and large relative to owner earnings, so its classification can materially change normalized OE and the valuation. The supplied record does not demonstrate how the workpapers treated it, however, and the full $7.765m is only an upper-bound sensitivity because the filing says construction was the primary, not exclusive, use of investing cash.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every 2024-2025 property-and-equipment outflow to the OE workpapers; separately identify facility construction, equipment replacement, moving costs, terminated rent and a filed or supportable maintenance-capex allowance, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Customer advances may be treated as distributable cash despite remaining obligations
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.532m total June 2026 deferred revenue, including $7.078m extended maintenance, $0.346m advances and $0.108m in-transit shipments; the entire balance is 12.7% of $59.08m cash but only 2.3% of $327m BASE equity value, or $0.58/share
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash while projected OE recognizes revenue and bears service costs associated with contract liabilities; an omission of those future costs could double-count part of the cash.
audit_findings.evidence: We record contract liabilities, or deferred revenue, when we have an obligation to provide a product or service to the customer and payment is received in advance of our performance.
audit_findings.explanation: No double count is demonstrated. Even deducting the entire deferred-revenue liability from cash—more severe than deducting the underlying fulfillment cost—would reduce BASE value from $25.33 to about $24.75/share and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $83.45 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $7.532m liability by obligation, estimate the associated fulfillment costs, and confirm that contract-liability releases and costs enter projected OE once; rerun the bridge only if that reconciliation identifies an omitted net obligation.

audit_findings.title: The 2026 pump transition makes FY2025 an uncertain steady-state anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; Q2 2026 pump revenue fell $1.760m or 21.5% year over year, Q2 gross margin fell 4.1 percentage points, while six-month total revenue rose $2.524m or 6.3% and operating income rose $1.408m or 11.5%
audit_findings.mechanism: Transition volume, pricing, launch inefficiencies, warranty costs and inventory provisions affect normalized OE and the appropriate growth path.
audit_findings.evidence: New MRidium 3860+ Pump System sales will be discontinued during 2026, with continued warranty and technical support continuing through applicable contracted periods.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing shows both transition pressure and offsetting company-wide growth, so FY2025 is not proven wrong as an anchor but is not established as steady state. The record cannot isolate the 3870 transition's sustainable OE effect or determine whether it warrants movement among the 0%, 5% and 8% cases.
audit_findings.action: Obtain 2026 orders, shipments, pricing, gross margin, warranty expense and inventory provisions by 3860+ and 3870; build a transition-adjusted run rate and rerun growth and margin scenarios if it differs materially from FY2025.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized software development could be omitted from reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.656m capitalized intangible outflow and $0.370m amortization in 2025; the full outflow equals 3.8% of the $17.1m anchor and, if permanently omitted, computes to about $10.3m or $0.80/share of BASE value
audit_findings.mechanism: Omitted capitalized development or patent cash outflows overstate OE; subtracting those outflows while also retaining related amortization understates OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We capitalize software development costs when the product reaches technological feasibility and cease capitalization when the product is ready for commercial sale.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that capitalized intangible spending exists, but not that the OE calculation omitted or double-counted it. Even the full 2025 outflow treated as a perpetual anchor error changes BASE value by only about 3.1%, far short of the $58.12/share gap between BASE value and market price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $0.656m 2025 and $0.324m first-half 2026 intangible outflows into OE, confirm that amortization is added back when the cash investment is deducted, and document maintenance versus growth development.

audit_findings.title: Tax timing may be embedded in the FY2025 anchor as a permanent run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.881m FY2025 tax expense versus $3.923m cash taxes, a $1.958m difference equal to 11.5% of the $17.1m anchor; perpetuating that difference computes to about $30.7m or $2.37/share of BASE value
audit_findings.mechanism: Using GAAP tax expense can understate near-term OE, while treating temporary cash-tax deductions as permanent can overstate normalized OE; deferred reversals affect future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: On July 4, 2025, the United States enacted The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (the “Bill”), which includes provisions that are expected to reduce our cash income tax payments over the next several years, with variability across periods, primarily due to additional depreciation deductions and the reinstatement of the immediate deduction of domestic research and development expenses.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed tax-expense and cash-tax difference is large enough to produce a material valuation sensitivity. This is not a demonstrated error because the supplied record does not show which tax measure entered the anchor or how future reversals were modeled; the higher 24.7% first-half 2026 effective rate also shows that FY2025's 20.7% rate is not automatically a stable cash-tax proxy.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor tax deduction to the return, cash-flow statement and deferred-tax roll-forward; separate permanent rate items from depreciation and R&D timing benefits, select a normalized long-run cash-tax burden, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Product-liability exposure can create an unmodeled claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed insurance limit is $5.0m with a $50,000 per-occurrence and $150,000 aggregate deductible
audit_findings.mechanism: An uninsured deductible, excluded claim, recall cost or loss above policy limits would reduce future OE or create a claim deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We currently have third-party product liability insurance with maximum coverage of $5,000,000; however, such coverage requires a substantial deductible that we must pay before becoming eligible to receive any insurance proceeds.
audit_findings.explanation: The exposure is forward-looking: the June 2026 filing reports no matter expected to have a material adverse effect, and the record supplies no present claim or estimable loss. Insurance terms establish possible retained exposure but do not quantify a valuation adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Monitor subsequent filings, adverse-event and recall data, claims notices, policy exclusions, aggregate-limit usage, indemnities and reserve changes; rerun OE or the bridge if a probable and estimable claim emerges.
